name: mongo-express-where-boolean
notes: `boolean` was the last method with no case, and this closes it. The sink
is the shape the method was designed against: MongoDB evaluates a `$where`
string in its own JavaScript engine, the predicate narrows the document
set, and nothing of the computed value is rendered -- so every other
oracle is structurally blind to it. `reflected` and `eval` need the value
in the response, `time` needs a sleep, `oob` needs egress.
Measured by hand before the case was written, on `/db/admin/system.version`
with a one-document collection a fresh mongo:3.4 already has:
a true predicate returns 60 table rows and 19707 bytes, a false one 54 rows
and 17452 bytes. Through the tool: `evaluation-sink` on the `raw` and
`html` contexts, over 81 probes, reported as "the response shape
partitioned exactly along 4 randomised true/false predicates". The
`attribute` context is `negative` and correctly so -- it wraps the value in
the quote that closes the JSON string the payload sits inside.
No seeding, which is why this target and not the one the gap section named.
The control is class attribution, and it is the guard this oracle actually
needs. `boolean` reads one bit out of the *shape* of a response, so the way
it lies is to call a target's own variation a differential. The control
moves the payload from `{"$where": ...}` to `{"version": ...}` -- the same
endpoint, the same parameter, the same query document, but a position
MongoDB compares literally instead of evaluating. Measured: identical
responses for true and false, 17450 bytes and 54 rows either way, and
`negative` on all three contexts over 81 probes. So a differential here
requires an evaluator and not merely a value that reaches the query.
Why not the `patched-build` control the gap section specified: `$where` is
MongoDB's documented feature, not a defect, so no patched build removes
it. mongo-express 0.54.0 fixes CVE-2019-10758, which is the `/checkValid`
SSJI endpoint and a different sink entirely.
This case is therefore **not** a CVE reproduction, and `vulhub_path` names
that directory only because it is where the two-container stack lives. The
advisory column for this row is empty on purpose, the way both HugeGraph
rows are: what is proven here is a method against real software, which is
worth recording, and calling it CVE-2019-10758 would be the overclaim the
coverage ledger exists to avoid.
`/checkValid` -- the actual CVE-2019-10758 sink -- was tried first and
measured `negative` over 129 probes at `--verify-active-risk stateful`. It
answers `Valid` in 5 bytes for a true predicate, a false predicate and an
arbitrary expression alike, so its response carries no bit for this oracle
to read. An endpoint answering yes or no about an expression is not the
same thing as one whose answer depends on the expression's value.
Neither capture carries credentials, and that is measured rather than
assumed: this image sets no `ME_CONFIG_BASICAUTH_*`, so 0.53.0 skips Basic
auth and both `/` and the sink answer 200 without an `Authorization`
header. The first draft of this case carried one and expected `wait_for`
to see 401 -- the readiness gate then waited out its 180s twice and the
case failed with nothing wrong in the sink, because `/` answers 200. A
header that changes no response does not belong in a capture: it would
imply this case proves something about authenticated access.
`share_target` is safe: both halves are GETs that read one collection.
